proofs.proof_tex:
Choose
\[
d=1,\qquad s=7,\qquad \delta=\frac14,\qquad
c_{\theta}=C_{\theta}=c_p=C_p=c_g=C_g=1,
\qquad v_{\kappa}=V_{\kappa}=\frac1{100},\qquad B=2.
\]
Then \(s=7>3(d+1)=6\), the four ordering requirements in
\(\texttt{def:model-class}\) hold, and
\[
\frac{c_{\theta}}2+\sqrt{v_{\kappa}}
=\frac12+\frac1{10}=\frac35<2=B.
\]
All polynomials used below, as well as the polynomials entering the definition
of \(L_0\), have finite \(C^s\) norms on their respective compact cubes.
Fix \(L\) at least as large as the maximum of those finitely many norms and
\(L_0\).  This verifies the compatibility requirements in
\(\texttt{def:model-class}\), including \(L\ge L_0\).

On a probability space let \(W\) and \(A\) be independent uniform random
variables on \([0,1]\), and let \(R\) be independent of \((W,A)\), with
\(\Pr(R=1)=\Pr(R=-1)=1/2\).  Define
\[
Y=A+\frac1{10}R+\frac1{10},
\]
and let \(P\) be the law of \((W,A,Y)\).  Since
\(0\le Y\le 6/5<B\), \(P\) satisfies
\(\texttt{ass:outcome-bound}\).  Direct conditioning gives the versions
\[
p(w)=1,\qquad g(a\mid w)=1,\qquad f(a)=1,
\]
and
\[
m(a,w)=a+\frac1{10},
\qquad
r(a,w)=\left(a+\frac1{10}\right)^2+\frac1{100}.
\]
Thus \(p\) and \(g\) integrate to one on their respective unit domains and
satisfy the two-sided bounds with
\(c_p=C_p=c_g=C_g=1\).  By the choice of \(L\), the displayed polynomial
versions satisfy \(\texttt{ass:p-smooth}\), \(\texttt{ass:g-smooth}\),
\(\texttt{ass:m-smooth}\), and \(\texttt{ass:r-smooth}\).  The definition of
\(\theta\) therefore yields, for every \(a\in[0,1]\),
\[
\theta(a)=\int_0^1m(a,w)p(w)\,dw=a+\frac1{10},
\qquad \theta'(a)=1.
\]
Consequently \(\theta\) is nondecreasing on \([0,1]\), as required by
\(\texttt{ass:monotone}\), and
\(c_{\theta}\le \theta'(a)\le C_{\theta}\) on
\(J=[1/4,3/4]\), as required by \(\texttt{ass:strict-slope}\).

The definitions of \(\sigma^2\) and \(e\) give
\[
\sigma^2(a,w)=r(a,w)-m(a,w)^2=\frac1{100},
\qquad e(a,w)=\frac{g(a\mid w)}{f(a)}=1.
\]
Using the definitions of \(\xi\) and \(\varepsilon\),
\[
\varepsilon
=\frac{Y-m(A,W)}{e(A,W)}
=\frac1{10}R.
\]
Hence, for every \(a\in J\),
\[
\kappa(a)=\mathbb E_P[\varepsilon^2\mid A=a]
=\frac1{100}=v_{\kappa}=V_{\kappa},
\]
which verifies \(\texttt{ass:variance}\).

It remains to construct two full-data witnesses for this same observed law.
For \(a\in[0,1]\), define the two potential-outcome processes
\[
Y_1(a)=a+\frac1{10}R+\frac1{10},
\qquad
Y_2(a)=a+\frac1{10}R+\frac1{10}\mathbf 1\{a=A\}.
\]
The maps \((a,A,R)\mapsto Y_j(a)\) are jointly Borel measurable: for
\(j=2\), this follows because the diagonal
\(\{(a,A):a=A\}\) is closed.  Each sample path is Borel measurable in
\(a\), and every coordinate evaluation is measurable; hence each
\(Y_j(\cdot)\) is a random element of the evaluation-sigma-field space
\(\mathcal Y_B\).  Moreover,
\[
-\frac1{10}\le Y_j(a)\le\frac65<B
\qquad (a\in[0,1],\ j\in\{1,2\}),
\]
so the potential-outcome coordinates have the stipulated range.  Let
\(P_j^{\mathrm F}\) be the law of
\((W,A,Y,Y_j(\cdot))\).  Its \((W,A,Y)\)-marginal is \(P\), which is
\(\texttt{ass:observed-marginal}\).  At the realized dose,
\[
Y_1(A)=A+\frac1{10}R+\frac1{10}=Y,
\qquad
Y_2(A)=A+\frac1{10}R+\frac1{10}\mathbf 1\{A=A\}=Y.
\]
Thus both full-data laws satisfy \(\texttt{ass:consistency}\).

Fix a deterministic \(a\in[0,1]\).  The treatment law is continuous, so
\(\Pr(A=a)=0\).  Therefore
\[
Y_1(a)=a+\frac1{10}R+\frac1{10}
\quad\text{and}\quad
Y_2(a)=a+\frac1{10}R
\quad\text{almost surely}.
\]
Each right-hand side is a function of \(R\) alone, while \(R\) is independent
of \((A,W)\).  In particular, for bounded Borel functions \(h\) and \(q\),
\[
\mathbb E\!\left[h\{Y_j(a)\}q(A)\mid W\right]
=\mathbb E\!\left[h\{Y_j(a)\}\mid W\right]
 \mathbb E\!\left[q(A)\mid W\right]
\quad\text{almost surely}.
\]
This factorization proves \(Y_j(a)\perp A\mid W\) for every deterministic
\(a\), so both witnesses satisfy \(\texttt{ass:exchangeability}\).

Because \(\mathbb E[R]=0\), jointly measurable conditional-mean versions are
\[
\mu^{\mathrm F}_1(a,w)=a+\frac1{10},
\qquad
\mu^{\mathrm F}_2(a,w)=a.
\]
For every \(w\), both functions are continuous in \(a\), and the preceding
almost-sure identities show that they are respectively versions of
\(\mathbb E_{P_j^{\mathrm F}}[Y_j(a)\mid W=w]\) for every fixed \(a\).
Thus \(\texttt{ass:potential-mean-continuity}\) holds for both witnesses.
All other conditions in \(\texttt{def:model-class}\) are properties of the
common observed marginal \(P\) and were verified above.  Consequently
\(P\in\mathcal M\), and both \(P_1^{\mathrm F}\) and
\(P_2^{\mathrm F}\) are admissible full-data witnesses for it.

Finally, for every \(a\in J\),
\[
\mathbb E_{P_1^{\mathrm F}}[Y_1(a)]
=a+\frac1{10}=\theta(a),
\qquad
\mathbb E_{P_2^{\mathrm F}}[Y_2(a)]
=a\ne a+\frac1{10}=\theta(a).
\]
The second process differs on the random diagonal \(a=A\).  That diagonal
has probability zero in every fixed-dose section, so it is invisible to
sectionwise exchangeability and to the continuous conditional-mean versions,
whereas consistency evaluates the process on exactly that diagonal.  The two
witnesses therefore establish the claimed failure of exact-dose causal
identification under the frozen model.

open_obligations.what_is_open: A theorem for the frozen learner requires a single measurable sample map, including a chosen kernel, boundary moment equations, a density-normalization map, and a convention on singular empirical Gram matrices.
open_obligations.obstruction: The frozen nuisance learner denotes a family of boundary-corrected local-polynomial procedures. Different members have different boundary matrices and exceptional-sample behavior, so a probability statement about that symbol is not well typed as a claim about one estimator.
open_obligations.attempted: The uniform bias and stochastic terms, the derivative cost, both advertised exponents, and stability under integration and well-conditioned quotient formation were derived for every fully specified regular implementation.
open_obligations.partial_result:
Put \(D=d+1\).  For any completely specified boundary local-polynomial implementation with a bounded compactly supported product kernel, degree at least \(\lceil s\rceil\), uniformly nonsingular population boundary moment matrices, and a declared measurable convention on singular empirical matrices, Taylor expansion and a uniform Bernstein-net argument give, for \(j\in\{0,1\}\),
\[
 \max_{1\le k\le K}
 \left\|\partial_a^j\widehat h_k-\partial_a^j h\right\|_\infty
 =O_P\!\left(h_n^{s-j}+
       \sqrt{\frac{\log n}{n h_n^{D+2j}}}\right).
\]
Here the display applies to the \(D\)-dimensional primitives, while the \(d\)-dimensional density estimator is no slower.  At the frozen bandwidth \(h_n=n^{-1/(2s)}\), the bias is at most \(n^{-1/2+j/(2s)}\), whereas the stochastic term is
\[
 n^{-1/2+(D+2j)/(4s)}\sqrt{\log n}.
\]
Consequently
\[
 \max_k\|\widehat h_k-h\|_\infty
 =O_P\!\left(n^{-\beta}\sqrt{\log n}\right),
 \qquad
 \beta=\frac12-\frac{d+1}{4s},
\]
and
\[
 \max_k\|\partial_a\widehat m_k-partial_a m\|_\infty
 =O_P\!\left(n^{-\beta_1}\sqrt{\log n}\right),
 \qquad
 \beta_1=\frac12-\frac{d+3}{4s}.
\]
The restriction \(s>3(d+1)\) yields
\[
 \beta>\frac12-\frac1{12}=\frac5{12},
 \qquad
 \beta_1>
 \frac12-\frac{d+3}{12(d+1)}
 =\frac{5d+3}{12(d+1)}>0.
\]
By \(\texttt{ass:p-bounds}\) and \(\texttt{ass:overlap}\), denominators are bounded away from zero.  The maps used to form products and quotients are therefore locally Lipschitz on the fixed bounded range, and integration over the unit covariate cube is a contraction in supremum norm.  In particular,
\[
 \|\widehat\theta'-\theta'\|_{\infty,J}
 \le
 \|\partial_a\widehat m-\partial_a m\|_\infty
 +\|\partial_a m\|_\infty\|\widehat p-p\|_1
 =O_P\!\left(n^{-\beta_1}\sqrt{\log n}\right).
\]
This establishes the advertised exponents for every implementation satisfying the displayed implementation conditions.  It does not establish the target for the frozen symbol \(\widehat\eta\), because that symbol does not choose a kernel or boundary moment system, does not specify the density-normalization map, and has no value on a singular empirical Gram matrix; hence it is not a single measurable map of the sample.

open_obligations.what_is_open: A uniform fold-conditional maximal inequality for the fitted validation-fold V-statistic and a proof that the four numerical transfer remainders imply stability of both optimized isotonic objectives remain missing.
open_obligations.obstruction: The validation-fold marginalization is a dependent V-statistic. In addition, optimized-value comparison needs common contact localization and slope envelopes, but neither property is a clause of the frozen transfer condition.
open_obligations.attempted: The product-bias, variance plug-in, and spatial-clock plug-in rates were derived; a Hoeffding decomposition gives the required polynomial scale for a fixed bounded marginalization kernel; and a deterministic optimized-value inequality reduces the remaining comparison to contact localization and slope control.
open_obligations.partial_result:
Conditional on the zeroth-order rates calculated in the preceding partial result, the definition of \(\mathfrak B_n\) gives
\[
 \mathfrak B_n=O_P(n^{-2\beta}\log n).
\]
Therefore
\[
 n^{5/6}(\log n)^{3/2}\mathfrak B_n
 =O_P\!\left(n^{5/6-2\beta}(\log n)^{5/2}\right)=o_P(1),
 \qquad
 \frac56-2\beta=-\frac16+\frac{d+1}{2s}<0,
\]
where the strict inequality follows from \(s>3(d+1)\).  Stable product, quotient, and integration inequalities, together with \(\texttt{ass:variance}\), similarly imply
\[
 \mathfrak K_n=O_P\!\left(n^{-\beta}\sqrt{\log n}\right)
\]
and
\[
 \left|\frac{\widehat{\mathcal V}_n}{\mathcal V(P)}-1\right|
 =O_P\!\left(n^{-\beta_1}\sqrt{\log n}
              +n^{-\beta}\sqrt{\log n}\right)=o_P(1).
\]
For the pure validation-fold marginalization term, let one fold have size \(N\asymp n\), let \(I\) have length \(h\), and let \(\phi\) be bounded and continuously differentiable.  The off-diagonal part of
\[
 \frac1{N^2}\sum_{i,j=1}^N
 \mathbf 1\{A_i\in I\}
 \left[\phi(A_i,W_j)-\int\phi(A_i,w)p(w)\,dw\right]
\]
has a zero first-coordinate projection, a second-coordinate projection of order \(h\), and a degenerate kernel with second moment of order \(h\).  Independence in \(\texttt{ass:iid}\) and the upper design-density bounds consequently give
\[
 O_P\!\left(\frac{h}{\sqrt n}+\frac{\sqrt h}{n}+\frac1n\right).
\]
At \(h=H_n=n^{-1/3}(\log n)^2\), multiplication by \(n^{2/3}\sqrt{\log n}\) sends each of these three terms to zero.

There is also a deterministic optimized-value inequality.  On a fixed interval, suppose both relevant monotone classes consist of functions bounded in absolute value by \(M_0\), and define
\[
 L_X(v)=\int v^2\,dt-2\int v\,dX.
\]
If \(\|X-\widetilde X\|_\infty\le\eta\), integration by parts and \(\operatorname{TV}(v)\le2M_0\) show
\[
 |L_X(v)-L_{\widetilde X}(v)|
 \le 8M_0\eta.
\]
Taking the infimum over the unconstrained class and the constrained subclass separately yields an LR optimized-value difference at most \(16M_0\eta\).  Thus the remaining transfer step is precisely to prove, uniformly at the moving level, common contact localization and a common slope envelope \(M_0\), and to prove the fitted-kernel version of the displayed uniform interval bound.  None of those properties is one of the four scalar clauses defining \(\mathsf G_n\).

open_obligations.what_is_open: A separable locally bounded version of the LR field and a quantitative common contact-radius tail for all constraint locations in a compact interval have not been constructed.
open_obligations.obstruction: Cubic-exponential localization of tilted argmin vertices does not exclude a remote supporting chord that changes either one-sided constrained GCM. The target's phrase concerning a tail sufficient for block independence also lacks a quantitative threshold to verify.
open_obligations.attempted: Brownian translation and affine GCM equivariance prove exact finite-dimensional stationarity. A Gaussian reflection and union-bound argument gives a cubic-exponential tail for every bounded family of tilted argmin vertices, thereby isolating remote supporting chords as the remaining geometric event.
open_obligations.partial_result:
The available exact property is finite-dimensional stationarity.  For \(x,t\in\mathbb R\), set
\[
 \mathbb W_x(t)=\mathbb W(x+t)-\mathbb W(x).
\]
Then
\[
 X(x+t)-X(x)-2xt=\mathbb W_x(t)+t^2.
\]
Affine equivariance of greatest convex minorants and the change of variable \(s=x+t\) give
\[
 D(x)=\Phi(\mathbb W_x),
\]
where \(\Phi\) is the origin-constrained Brownian--GCM energy whenever that energy is defined.  Stationarity of Brownian increments therefore implies
\[
 (D(x_1+h),\ldots,D(x_m+h))
 \stackrel{d}{=}(D(x_1),\ldots,D(x_m))
\]
for every finite collection \(x_1,ldots,x_m\) and every \(h\in\mathbb R\).

One can also localize ordinary tilted argmin vertices.  For each fixed \(C<\infty\), Gaussian reflection bounds on every interval \([j,j+1]\), followed by a summable union bound, give constants \(c_1,c_2,R_0>0\) such that
\[
 \Pr\!\left{exists |c|\le C:\
   \operatorname*{argmin}_{t\in\mathbb R}\{X(t)-ct\}
   \not\subset[-R,R]\right}
 \le c_1e^{-c_2R^3},
 \qquad R\ge R_0.
\]
Indeed, for \(R\ge2C\), a minimizing point with \(|t|\ge R\) must satisfy \(W(t)\le-t^2/2\), because the value at zero is zero.  On \([j,j+1]\), this event is contained in the union of \(\{W(j)\le-j^2/4\}\) and \(\{\inf_{0\le r\le1}[W(j+r)-W(j)]\le-j^2/4\}\), whose probabilities are bounded respectively by constants times \(e^{-c j^3}\) and \(e^{-c j^4}\); summing over \(j\ge R-1\) and treating the negative half-line identically proves the display.  The same argument also gives \(W(t)/t^2\to0\) almost surely and hence coercivity of every bounded linear tilt.

This vertex bound does not control a remote supporting chord of either one-sided constrained GCM.  Consequently it neither proves that the constrained and unconstrained slopes have jointly compact difference support uniformly over a continuum of constraint locations nor constructs a separable locally bounded version of \(D\).

open_obligations.what_is_open: The infinite-domain small-noise principle, sharp one-cluster expansion, additive tail ratio, positive runs intensity, uniform rare-block law, short-range anticlustering, marked Poisson limit, Gumbel law, and growing-window padding and mesh approximation remain unproved.
open_obligations.obstruction: Exact Brownian scaling and a variational action bracket do not yield the translation-mode prefactor or constant-order logarithmic-tail accuracy. Long-range truncation does not imply short-range anticlustering, and no frozen or cited theorem supplies the peak-mark law for this nonlinear Brownian--GCM energy field.
open_obligations.attempted: The exact small-noise scaling, Hilbert-projection action lower bound, and compactly supported plateau witness with unit LR energy and action nine-eighths were checked equation by equation. These calculations identify the candidate speed and a nontrivial action bracket but stop before any sharp probability asymptotic.
open_obligations.partial_result:
Let \(\Phi(h)\) be the origin-constrained LR energy generated by \(t^2+h(t)\), for an absolutely continuous \(h\) with \(h(0)=0\) and \(h'\in L^2(\mathbb R)\).  For \(b>0\), define \(h_b(t)=b^2h(t/b)\).  Spatial and affine equivariance of the constrained and unrestricted GCMs, followed by the substitution \(t=bs\), give the exact homogeneities
\[
 \Phi(h_b)=b^3\Phi(h),
 \qquad
 \frac12\int_{\mathbb R}h_b'(t)^2\,dt
 =b^3\frac12\int_{\mathbb R}h'(t)^2\,dt.
\]
Brownian scaling with \(b=u^{1/3}\) therefore yields the exact identity
\[
 \Pr\{D(0)>u\}
 =\Pr\{\Phi(u^{-1/2}\mathbb W)>1\}.
\]
Thus \(u\), rather than a power inferred from an analogy with slope extremes, is the candidate small-noise speed.

Define the deterministic action
\[
 I_\star=inf\left\{
  \frac12\int_{\mathbb R}h'(t)^2\,dt:\Phi(h)\ge1
 \right\}.
\]
On a finite interval containing the contact set, let \(\mathcal C_0\subset\mathcal C\) be the zero-constrained and unrestricted monotone-slope cones.  Since the baseline slope \(2t\) belongs to \(\mathcal C_0\), the Hilbert projection identity gives
\[
 \Phi(h)
 =\operatorname{dist}^2(2t+h',\mathcal C_0)
  -\operatorname{dist}^2(2t+h',\mathcal C)
 \le\|h'\|_2^2.
\]
After increasing the finite interval through the stabilized contact set, this proves \(I_\star\ge1/2\).

For the converse deterministic witness, put \(k=4^{1/3}\), \(a=k/4\), and
\[
 h'(t)=(k-2t)\mathbf 1\{-a\le t\le k/2\}.
\]
Then \(2t+h'(t)\) is nondecreasing and equals \(k\) on \([-a,k/2]\).  Its unrestricted isotonic projection is itself, while its zero-constrained projection replaces the plateau by zero on \([-a,0]\).  Hence
\[
 \Phi(h)=ak^2=\frac{k^3}{4}=1
\]
and, by direct integration,
\[
 \frac12\int_{\mathbb R}h'(t)^2\,dt
 =\frac12\int_{-a}^{k/2}(k-2t)^2\,dt
 =\frac{(k+2a)^3}{12}
 =\frac98.
\]
Therefore
\[
 \frac12\le I_\star\le\frac98.
\]
The same witness is compactly supported, so finite-window PAVA recovers it once the window contains \([-a,k/2]\).  These exact identities do not constitute an infinite-domain large-deviation principle.  Even such a principle would determine only a logarithmic rate; it would not determine the translation-mode prefactor, an additive \(o(1)\) expansion of \(-\log\lambda(u)\), the compact-additive tail ratio, short-range anticlustering, marked-Poisson convergence, or the padded-grid error.  In particular, none of those conclusions follows from stationarity or from the action bracket.

open_obligations.what_is_open: A measurable uniform coupling of the growing-domain oracle continuum LR statistic to the canonical maximum, followed by optimized stability for the cross-fitted statistic, remains unavailable.
open_obligations.obstruction: The claim requires a sorted-residual strong approximation, interpolation of rank and variance clocks, common constrained and unconstrained contact localization, local coefficient freezing with overlap gluing, and empirical dose-cell comparison at a moving logarithmic threshold.
open_obligations.attempted: The exact local cube-root scale was derived, all required divisions were justified from overlap, slope, and variance bounds, and its inverse was integrated to obtain the stated spatial-volume clock exactly. A global quadratic approximation cannot replace the missing local gluing argument.
open_obligations.partial_result:
For \(a\in J\), define the local dose scale
\[
 h_n(a)=\left\{\frac{4\kappa(a)}{n f(a)\theta'(a)^2}\right\}^{1/3}.
\]
By \(\texttt{ass:p-normalization}\) and \(\texttt{ass:overlap}\),
\[
 c_g\le f(a)=\int g(a\mid w)p(w)\,dw\le C_g.
\]
Together with \(\texttt{ass:strict-slope}\) and \(\texttt{ass:variance}\), this makes \(h_n(a)\) positive and gives constants \(0<c<C<\infty\), depending only on the fixed model constants, such that
\[
 c\le n^{1/3}h_n(a)\le C
\]
uniformly in \(a\in J\) and \(P\in\mathcal M\).  Direct algebra gives
\[
 \frac1{h_n(a)}
 =n^{1/3}\left\{\frac{f(a)\theta'(a)^2}{4\kappa(a)}\right\}^{1/3}
\]
and therefore
\[
 \int_J\frac{da}{h_n(a)}
 =n^{1/3}\int_J
   \left\{\frac{f(a)\theta'(a)^2}{4\kappa(a)}\right\}^{1/3}da
 =T_n(P).
\]
Consequently
\[
 a\longmapsto\int_{\inf J}^{a}h_n(v)^{-1}\,dv
\]
is a bi-Lipschitz canonical coordinate that maps \(J\) to an interval of length exactly \(T_n(P)\).  This proves the spatial-volume clock and all divisions used in it.  It does not construct the claimed coupling: that requires a sorted-residual strong approximation, interpolation of the empirical rank and variance clocks, common contact localization for both optimized problems, locally uniform coefficient freezing with overlap gluing, and comparison of both one-sided limits in every empirical dose cell at a threshold of order \(\log n\).

open_obligations.what_is_open: Nominal analytic and simulated calibration remains conditional on uniform clock consistency, the canonical Gumbel law, observed-law transfer, random-horizon padded-grid approximation, and quantile anti-concentration.
open_obligations.obstruction: Relative clock consistency would justify substitution into an already established centering and scale, but it cannot create the missing limit law or identify finite padded-simulation quantiles with continuum quantiles.
open_obligations.attempted: The uniform positive lower bound for the spatial volume, inverse-centering mean-value calculation, asymptotic scale substitution, and conditional empirical-distribution error for the prescribed number of simulations were derived.
open_obligations.partial_result:
For every \(P\in\mathcal M\), \(\texttt{ass:p-normalization}\), \(\texttt{ass:overlap}\), \(\texttt{ass:strict-slope}\), and \(\texttt{ass:variance}\) imply
\[
 \mathcal V(P)
 \ge |J|\left\{\frac{c_gc_\theta^2}{4V_\kappa}\right\}^{1/3}>0.
\]
Hence \(\inf_{P\in\mathcal M}T_n(P)\to\infty\), so the deterministic eventual regime is nonempty for all sufficiently large \(n\).  Conditional on the still-unproved uniform clock consistency
\[
 \widehat{\mathcal V}_n/\mathcal V(P)=1+o_P(1),
\]
one has \(\log\{\widehat T_n/T_n(P)\}=o_P(1)\) and \(\Pr_P\{\widehat T_n\ge T_0\}\to1\) uniformly.  On that event, the mean-value theorem applied to \(\mathcal E_\star(b(T))=\log T\) gives
\[
 \frac{b(\widehat T_n)-b(T_n(P))}{a(T_n(P))}
 =\frac{\mathcal E_\star'(b(T_n(P)))}
        {\mathcal E_\star'(\widetilde b_n)}
   \log\frac{\widehat T_n}{T_n(P)},
\]
where \(\widetilde b_n\) lies between the two centerings.  If the canonical expansion asserted by \(\texttt{thm:canonical-excursion}\) were available, then both centerings would diverge and
\[
 \mathcal E_\star'(u)=\beta_\star+\frac{\gamma_\star}{u},
 \qquad
 \frac{b(\widehat T_n)-b(T_n(P))}{a(T_n(P))}=o_P(1),
\]
while
\[
 \frac{a(\widehat T_n)}{a(T_n(P))}
 =\frac{\mathcal E_\star'(b(T_n(P)))}
        {\mathcal E_\star'(b(\widehat T_n))}
 \longrightarrow1.
\]
Thus clock substitution is valid once the missing expansion and clock consistency have been proved.  Conditionally on the data, the Dvoretzky--Kiefer--Wolfowitz bound for the prescribed \(n^2\) independent simulated maxima yields uniform empirical-distribution error \(O_P(n^{-1})\).  That empirical bound alone supplies neither the random-horizon padded-grid approximation nor the anti-concentration needed to transfer simulated quantiles to the continuum maximum.

open_obligations.what_is_open: The deterministic interval and threshold-crossing inversion is complete, but its claimed nominal limiting coverage is exactly the unresolved probability assertion in feasible calibration.
open_obligations.obstruction: Convexity and set-image arguments preserve coverage of the common LR event; they cannot prove that the proposed critical value gives that event the nominal limiting probability.
open_obligations.attempted: The constrained optimized value was proved convex, the simultaneous band event was identified exactly with the supremum event, and the true monotone curve was mapped to its threshold crossing under the stated endpoint conventions.
open_obligations.partial_result:
Fix \(k\in\{1,ldots,n\}\) and define
\[
 L_k(t)=\min_{v\in\mathcal C_n,\,v_k=t}
          \sum_{i=1}^n(Z_{(i)}-v_i)^2.
\]
The feasible set is nonempty because it contains the constant vector \(t\mathbf 1\).  If \(v^{(1)}\) and \(v^{(2)}\) are feasible at \(t_1\) and \(t_2\), then, for every \(\lambda\in[0,1]\),
\[
 \lambda v^{(1)}+(1-\lambda)v^{(2)}\in\mathcal C_n,
 \qquad
 [\lambda v^{(1)}+(1-\lambda)v^{(2)}]_k
 =\lambda t_1+(1-\lambda)t_2.
\]
Convexity of squared loss and passage to infima show that \(L_k\) is convex.  Therefore
\[
 Q_n(a,t)=L_{k(a)}(t)
 -\min_{v\in\mathcal C_n}\sum_{i=1}^n(Z_{(i)}-v_i)^2
\]
is convex in \(t\), and each sublevel set \(\mathcal C_n(a)\) is an interval, allowing the empty interval and \(\mathbb R\).  Positivity of \(\widehat\kappa(a)\) gives the exact event identity
\[
 \{\theta(a)\in\mathcal C_n(a)\text{ for every }a\in J\}
 =\left\{\sup_{a\in J}
          \frac{Q_n(a,\theta(a))}{\widehat\kappa(a)}
          \le\widehat q_{n,\alpha}\right\}
 =\{S_n(\theta)\le\widehat q_{n,\alpha}\}.
\]
On this event, \(\theta\) is an admissible nondecreasing selector by \(\texttt{ass:monotone}\), so the image in \(\texttt{def:crossing-set}\) contains its threshold crossing \(\tau_\zeta\), including the empty-set and endpoint conventions.  The inversion therefore loses no coverage relative to the common LR event.  It cannot determine that event's limiting probability; that is exactly the unresolved assertion in \(\texttt{thm:feasible-calibration}\).

open_obligations.what_is_open: The constant-coefficient clock and fixed-location identities are proved, but the proposition's invocation of the three growing-domain inference theorems cannot be certified while those theorems remain open.

Suppose \(f(a)=f_0\), \(\theta'(a)=r_0\), and \(\kappa(a)=\kappa_0\) on \(J\).  Substitution into \(\texttt{def:spatial-clock}\) gives the exact identities
\[
 \mathcal V(P)=|J|\left(\frac{f_0r_0^2}{4\kappa_0}\right)^{1/3},
 \qquad
 T_n(P)=n^{1/3}|J|
 \left(\frac{f_0r_0^2}{4\kappa_0}\right)^{1/3}.
\]
The canonical coordinate has constant derivative
\[
 n^{1/3}\left(\frac{f_0r_0^2}{4\kappa_0}\right)^{1/3}
\]
and hence maps \(J\) affinely to an interval of exactly the displayed length.  At one fixed dose, translation places the constraint at the origin; \(\texttt{def:canonical-field}\) then gives the marginal functional \(D(0)\).  These are exact algebraic reductions.  They do not prove the proposition's further invocation of the growing-domain excursion, observed-law transfer, and feasible-calibration theorems.
